beats.text: Wood is found, the fire is coaxed up, and the day is set down where everyone can see it.
Nobody says much at first. Then somebody always does.
He sets down what he is carrying, and waits for you to reach him.
A cabin hand off some ship that never came back sits on the lip of the well, kicking his heels, a cutlass too big for him across his knees.
He sees the swords and does not run, which tells you something about this year.
The watchman has been awake a long time. He hears the armour before he sees it.
The duckboards flex under you, and the wizard does not look up until they stop.
He has been counting something in the water, and he has lost the count.
The axe comes down once more, unhurried, before anyone acknowledges you.
He rests the haft on his shoulder and waits, which is its own kind of question.
He is facing the water, and he keeps facing it while your whole company walks up the shingle behind him.
Gilt armour in a bailey with nobody in it. He straightens anyway, out of habit older than the habit is useful.
